questions.question: The live baseline has 120 streams sampled at 8 frames per second. A balanced replica processes 320 frames per second, and the fleet should stay at or below 70% steady utilization. What is the minimum planned replica count before considering a zone loss?
options: 3 replicas, because 960 divided by 320 equals 3.
4 replicas, because one extra replica always provides enough headroom.
5 replicas, because ceil(960 / (320 x 0.70)) equals 5.
8 replicas, because every stream needs its own replica.
questions.explanation: The 70% operating target means each replica is planned for 224 frames per second, so 960 / 224 requires five replicas after rounding up.

questions.question: Which record best preserves the lesson's reproducibility invariant for a returned detection?
options: Only the predicted class and confidence score.
The input reference, preprocessing version, release manifest, threshold or policy version, and prediction outcome.
The current GPU utilization and the user's browser version.
A copy of whichever model was latest when the operator reviewed the alert.
questions.explanation: A prediction is auditable only when the exact input reference and all versioned transformations and decisions that created it can be reconstructed.

questions.question: Why should resize mode, color conversion, normalization, and frame sampling be bundled with a model release?
options: They reduce object-storage cost regardless of the model.
They are presentation details that do not affect detector output.
They are part of the model contract; changing them can create training-serving skew even when the weights are unchanged.
They allow a failed policy check to reuse a prediction from another tenant.
questions.explanation: The detector learned against a particular input representation. A different transform can shift scores and boxes, so it must be versioned and evaluated with the weights.

questions.question: A candidate improves aggregate mAP but reduces night-camera recall by 4.8 points and has population stability index 0.29. What is the right release decision?
options: Expand immediately because aggregate mAP improved.
Lower the confidence threshold and ignore the drift signal.
Hold the customer-facing release, investigate the slice and drift, and use shadow comparison if needed.
Delete night-camera examples from the evaluation set because they are harder.
questions.explanation: A required slice regression and an input-drift breach are hard release failures. Threshold tuning cannot prove that the candidate remains reliable under the shifted condition.

questions.question: What is the most defensible response when accelerator pressure threatens the live deadline?
options: Let batching wait without a cap until every frame receives the largest model.
Use an explicitly approved lower sampling rate or model tier for eligible work, queue non-live work, and record the fallback reason.
Skip authentication and preprocessing to save time.
Reuse a result from a different tenant with a similar camera scene.
questions.explanation: A bounded, observable fallback preserves policy and lineage while protecting the live deadline. Validation and tenant isolation are never capacity-shedding candidates.

questions.question: Why is an ignored operator alert not automatically a negative training label?
options: It proves the detector was correct because the alert was delivered.
It may reflect a wrong detection, a noisy policy, an overloaded operator, or an unavailable camera, so review context is needed before labeling.
It can never be stored for audit because alerts are too small.
It means the detector should be retrained synchronously on the next request.
questions.explanation: Production feedback is delayed and confounded by the workflow. Keep provenance and review evidence rather than turning an ambiguous absence of action into model ground truth.
